absent: Locking and concurrency rules for aggregate lists, counts, hash access and identifier allocation.
Semantics of delta checking, delta creation, parent lookup and assignment, and statistics increment and decrement.
Full structure layouts for manager, object, hint, statistics and pool head and slot beyond observed fields.
Hash initialization, insertion, lookup and removal contracts and their error codes beyond observed call sites.
Tracing, memory ordering and RCU protection requirements outside the teardown raw access notes.
Test world setup, key type, buffer contents and expected counts.

Root and delta private data ownership and lifetime beyond create and destroy pairing.

findings.text: Aggregation manager offers creation from a callback table with optional prior hints and opaque context, plus destruction. Creation fails on incomplete callbacks or allocation failure. Destruction releases the identifier allocator and hash storage, drops the hint reference when present, and frees the manager.

Clients acquire an aggregated object by key and later release it. Acquisition reuses an existing entry with an added reference when the key matches, otherwise builds a new entry and reports failures as error pointers. Release updates statistics and drops a reference, destroying the entry when the count reaches zero.

Statistics snapshots can be taken for a live aggregate and for a hint set, then released. Each snapshot copies per entry counters, records root status and root totals, orders entries deterministically, and is freed by its release operation.

An optimization hint set can be derived from a populated aggregate using a selectable algorithm, and later released under reference counting. Derivation validates complete coverage of live objects. Final release flushes all hint nodes and destroys hash storage before freeing the set.

Resizable hash storage offers plain teardown and general teardown with optional per element release. Plain teardown delegates with no callback. General teardown synchronizes deferred work, walks current and successor tables, optionally releases each element, and frees table memory including nested levels.

Primary library entry points are manager creation, keyed acquisition and release, live and hint statistics snapshot and release, and hint derivation and release. Hash teardown entry delegates to the general teardown path.

Per CPU pool slot initialization prepares a ring mask from capacity and fills entries from a contiguous object area, optionally invoking a caller initializer per object and accounting the pool total. Initializer failure aborts the fill and propagates the error.
Manager creation requires five callbacks covering root lifetime and delta checking plus lifetime. Absence triggers a warning and an invalid argument failure.

Each object carries a reference count raised on successful lookup or creation and lowered on release. Transition to zero is the sole trigger for removal from list and hash followed by finalization and freeing.

Live objects are present in both a list and a keyed hash with a manager count. Creation adds to both and increments. Destruction removes from both and decrements. Teardown while objects remain is treated as unexpected and warned against.

Root identifiers use an allocator only when hints exist, otherwise an invalid sentinel is stored. Hinted roots are confined to the hinted value while unhinted roots start after the hinted root total and extend to the maximum. Allocation failure propagates and successful creation pairs allocation with later release.

Initialization prefers hints when a hint node matches the key. A hint without a parent becomes a root. A hint with a parent attempts parent reuse and attachment, and attachment failure clears the hint found flag and falls back to non hint processing without failing, while parent lookup failure propagates.
Snapshot ordering places root entries before non root entries, then orders by delta user count descending, then by user count descending.

Hint nodes carry user counts derived from the source object, with child creation adding the child user total to the parent delta total. Fresh roots draw sequential identifiers from a hint local counter and are flagged as roots. Node creation inserts into hash and list and increments the hint node total.

Hint sets are reference counted starting at one, incremented when adopted by a new manager, decremented on manager teardown and explicit release, with storage reclaimed only when the count reaches zero.

Temporary node weight equals its own user total plus user totals of all feasible successors that remain uncrossed. Maximum selection scans all uncrossed nodes, updates on greater or equal so ties favor later positions, and reports negative one when none remain.
Test doubles maintain a world with root and delta totals. Creation allocates an entry, copies key material and samples a buffer while incrementing. Destruction decrements and frees.

General hash teardown must not acquire the table mutex because deferred rehash work already orders that mutex before filesystem reclaim, so reclaim path callers would close a circular dependency. It instead synchronizes interrupt and workqueue activity and accesses tables with raw dereference.

Temporary optimization storage holds a dense node array and a square bit matrix. Each node stores a back pointer to a live object and a crossed out flag. The matrix records directed delta feasibility between every ordered pair excluding self pairs, indexed by a row major function of the two positions.

Optimization algorithms are represented by a structure holding a single fill operation taking a hint set and a live aggregate. One constant instance implements simple greedy behavior and is published through a small table indexed by algorithm selector.

Hash parameters for live objects and hint nodes store key length from operation object size plus offsets to key storage and hash linkage within their respective entries. Live entries key on embedded object bytes and hint entries key on their own object bytes.

Nested hash teardown derives fanout from table size and nesting depth, reaches the top table without RCU protection because it is fixed with the depth, and recurses based on page size and pointer size. Plain tables free directly after nested levels are reclaimed.

Pool slot state observed here includes a mask derived from capacity, an entry ring with tail and last positions, and linkage to pool capacity, object size and total object count. Object memory follows the entry array contiguously.

Object birth follows lookup then create then initialize then hash insert then list add. Initialization stages are hint attempt, existing parent aggregation attempt, then root creation. Death follows reference drop to zero then list and hash removal then finalization. Finalization branches to parent release with delta teardown for non roots and to root teardown with callback and identifier release for roots.

Greedy hint construction builds the feasibility graph, then loops selecting the highest weight uncrossed node as a new root hint and attaching all still uncrossed outgoing neighbours as its children, marking each consumed node crossed out until none remain, then destroys the graph.

General hash teardown starts at the current table and follows successor tables until none remain. When a release callback is present each bucket chain is walked to its terminator with periodic rescheduling, handling both single entries and chained list entries by invoking the callback on each containing object.

Three unexpected states are flagged with warnings: incomplete callback table at creation, teardown while objects remain, and hint derivation whose node total differs from the live object total, the last also converting to invalid argument failure.

Allocation and insertion failures unwind in reverse order: root creation failure releases the just allocated identifier, object creation hash failure finalizes before freeing, and hint derivation failure flushes partial nodes and destroys hash storage before freeing the hint set.
A distinguished invalid root identifier value is used when no hints are configured.
A selector value identifies the simple greedy optimization algorithm within the algorithm table used by hint derivation.
